min_wage: The federal minimum wage should be $20 an hour or more and rise with inflation every year.
The federal minimum wage should be about $15 an hour and rise with inflation every year.
The federal minimum wage should be raised to about $10 to $12 an hour.
The federal minimum wage should stay at $7.25 an hour.
There should be no federal minimum wage; states and employers should set pay.
min_wage_jobs: Raise the minimum wage to $15 quickly. Higher pay for millions is worth losing some low-wage jobs.
Raise the minimum wage to $15 over several years, accepting some job losses but trying to keep them small.
Raise the minimum wage only part of the way to $15, or only in places where living costs are high.
Don't raise the minimum wage, because the lost jobs fall hardest on the least experienced workers.
right_to_work: Union contracts that require every covered worker to pay fees should be allowed everywhere, overriding state right-to-work laws.
Each state should keep deciding whether union contracts can require fees.
Union contracts that require fees should be banned in every state.
union_organizing: A union should be recognized as soon as most workers sign cards, and employers who interfere should face large fines.
Union votes should happen faster, and employers who break the rules should pay bigger fines.
The rules for forming a union should stay as they are.
Unions should be harder to keep: workers should have to vote again every few years to keep their union.
public_unions: Government workers like teachers should be able to bargain through unions and to go on strike.
Government workers should be able to bargain through unions, but not to strike.
Government workers' unions should bargain only over wages, not benefits or work rules.
Government workers shouldn't be able to bargain as a group at all.
paid_leave: Federal law should guarantee 12 weeks or more of paid leave for a new child or serious illness, paid for with a payroll tax.
Federal law should guarantee a shorter paid leave, about 4 to 6 weeks.
Paid leave shouldn't be required, but employers who offer it should get a tax credit.
The federal government should stay out of paid leave and leave it to employers and states.
sick_days: Every employer should have to give workers at least 7 paid sick days a year.
Employers with more than 50 workers should have to give paid sick days; smaller ones shouldn't.
Paid sick days shouldn't be required; states and employers should decide.
gig_workers: App-based drivers and delivery workers should count as employees, with minimum wage, overtime and benefits.
App-based workers should be a new category, with guaranteed minimum pay and some benefits but flexible hours.
App-based workers should stay independent contractors, without employee pay rules or benefits.

s: Strong rules to protect workers, consumers and the environment come first, even if prices rise and fewer businesses start.
I lean toward stronger protections, even at some cost to prices and new businesses.
I lean toward fewer rules, even if more workers and consumers get hurt by unsafe practices.
Fewer rules come first, so businesses grow and prices stay low, even if more people are harmed by unsafe practices.
regulation_tradeoff.torn: I weigh stronger protections and fewer rules about equally.

s: New products should be proven safe before they're sold, even if useful ones are delayed for years.
I lean toward proving new products safe first, even with some delays.
I lean toward allowing new products and fixing problems as they come up.
New products should be allowed on sale and problems dealt with later, even if some people are harmed first.
precaution_tradeoff.torn: I weigh testing first and allowing first about equally.

big_company_breakup: Companies that control most of their market should be broken up, even if their prices are low.
Dominant companies should be broken up only when it's proven they hurt consumers, workers or competitors.
Leave dominant companies as they are, but stop them from buying their rivals.
Leave dominant companies alone; being big usually means they're good at what they do, and new competitors will come.
merger_rules: Most large mergers should be blocked unless the companies prove the merger will help customers and workers.
Each large merger should be reviewed, and blocked if it's likely to raise prices or cut wages.
Most mergers should be approved unless they'd clearly raise prices.
The government should rarely step in; companies should be free to merge.
bank_rules: The rules should be much stricter, including breaking up the largest banks.
Large banks should have to keep more of their own money as a cushion against losses.
Rules on large banks should stay about as strict as today.
Rules on large banks should be looser than today so they can lend more.
bailouts: If a company's collapse would cause a recession, the government should take it over and run it until it can be sold or closed down.
The government should lend a failing giant money to survive, with strict conditions, as in 2008.
The government should protect customers' insured deposits and let the company itself fail.
The government should let it fail with no help at all, even if that causes a recession.
licensing: More jobs should require a government license, to protect customers.
Job licensing should stay about where it is.
Licenses should be required only where health or safety is clearly at risk, like electricians, not interior designers.
Most license requirements should go; customers can rely on reviews and private certifications.
price_controls: The government should cap prices on essentials like food and gas when inflation is high, not just after disasters.
Sharp price hikes on essentials should be banned only during declared emergencies, like after a hurricane.
Businesses should be free to raise prices on essentials, even after disasters, because high prices draw in more supply.
economic_system: Most major industries should be owned by the public or by the people who work in them.
Businesses should be mostly private, but government should run key industries like energy and health care.
Businesses should be private, with strong government rules and a large safety net.
Businesses should be private, with modest rules and a basic safety net.
Businesses should be private and markets free, with as little government as possible.
public_ownership: Government should own and run most utilities like electricity, railroads and internet service.
Government should run some utilities, where private companies haven't provided good, affordable service.
Government should run utilities only where no private company provides them.
Private companies, not government, should run utilities like electricity, railroads and internet service.
workers_on_boards: Workers at companies with over 1,000 employees should elect about half of the board.
Workers at companies with over 1,000 employees should elect about a third of the board.
Companies can choose to put elected workers on their board, but it shouldn't be required.
noncompetes: Employers shouldn't be able to stop any worker from taking a job with a competitor.
Only top executives can be bound by agreements not to work for a competitor.
Agreements not to work for a competitor are fine, but should last a year or less.
Agreements not to work for a competitor are fine; both sides signed the contract.
right_to_repair: Makers of most products should have to make parts, tools and manuals available to owners and independent repair shops.
Makers should have to provide repair parts and information only for products where repair matters most, like cars and farm equipment.
Companies should decide for themselves whether to provide repair parts and information.
farm_subsidies: Federal payments and subsidized insurance for farmers should be expanded.
Federal payments and subsidized insurance for farmers should stay about as they are.
Farm payments and subsidized insurance should go only to small and mid-size farms.
Federal payments and subsidized insurance for farmers should be phased out.
business_incentives: States and cities should offer tax breaks to bring in factories and offices, because they bring jobs.
Tax breaks for companies are fine only with firm job guarantees and repayment if the company leaves.
States and cities should be banned from offering tax breaks to attract companies.
fed_independence: The Federal Reserve should set interest rates on its own, with no pressure from the president or Congress.
The Federal Reserve should set interest rates, but Congress should review its decisions more closely.
A president should be able to tell the Federal Reserve what interest rates to set.
infrastructure: The federal government should spend much more than today on roads, bridges, water systems and the power grid, paid for by borrowing or taxes.
The federal government should spend somewhat more than today on infrastructure.
Federal infrastructure spending should stay about the same.
The federal government should spend less on infrastructure and leave more to states and private companies.
